observations: Rails are the densest crate terrain: 12 crates in ~25 s on rail 1, 14 in ~24 s on rail 2 (about one per 2 s vs one per 4-5 s on foot).

Rail crates live at three heights (above, at, below the rail); the obstacle decides the posture, the first crate of each posture sits where the dodge puts you, tests put it on the far side of the obstacle.
No TNT or Nitro ever sits on a rail; rail lethality comes only from authored obstacles, so rail crates are pure reward.
Each rail verb (HANG, SWITCH RAIL, SWING) is prompted once and paid immediately with crates only that verb reaches.
Checkpoints bracket the rails and never sit on them: C2 on the entry ledge, C3 at rail 1's landing, C4 at rail 2's dismount.
Slow puzzle rooms (slam lesson, slam pyramid, ! bridge) sit between the two speed sections; the ! bridge leads straight onto rail 2.
Explosives teach immunity: TNT clears wood but not iron-bound (S5-b, S10-d); TNT counts, so the bonus uses TNT stacks as crates.
The phase mask is taught at the start, removed for the rails, and returned for the bonus and finale.
Count traps orbit the bonus pad (left tyres, checkpoint, right tyres); high crates guarded by a tool are the other trap family (S2-a, S3-c, S5-c, F-a).
All 6 Nitros sit in the phase sections and count only when the exit detonator fires.
Crates signpost routes: the Aku crate marks the hidden left path, a ? on a car hood marks rail 2's entrance, a W on a metal platform marks rail 1's exit.

geometryObservations: Rails cannot be fallen off (GP), so all rail danger is authored obstacles: four boards and a pillar on rail 1; alternating boards, an oncoming cart and tower barriers on rail 2. On rail 1 the obstacle spacing compresses from 9.5 s to 2.5 s.

Each rail adds an axis: rail 1 is vertical (above, on and below the line, in a side view), rail 2 is lateral (twin rails in a chase view) and then vertical again at the towers (side view). The camera always shows the axis being tested.
Rail gaps are few and readable: one break at a pillar on rail 1, two or three rail-to-rail jumps near the top of rail 2, each previewed by a crate (above the break, on the line).
Both rails end in an automatic launch onto a checkpoint pad (~ 2 x 2 u for C3; the C4 deck): speed sections end with a guaranteed landing and a save.
The phase mask makes gaps: a phase bridge span, a platform field with half the squares solid, phase columns and pillars. Gap widths stay <= 2-3 u; the difficulty is when to toggle.
Shark sand is a delayed-lethal floor under ~ 1 u drum tops: the smallest footing in the level is paired with a floor that kills if you stop, which creates its first no-stop sequence.
Explosives sit on landings: the Nitro mesas (G-S1-d) put the hazard where you land, and the Nitro is introduced with a text prompt and a phase escape.
Slow, wide puzzle decks follow each speed section: pads with 1 u gaps, then the 6 x 4 u slam deck after rail 1; the C4 deck after rail 2.
The narrowest lane (the 1 u outline bridge) is a CHOKE built by the player's own switch, placed right before rail 2.

Enemies in this 2084 level deny areas more than they block lanes: sand sharks, a bomb thrower above a walkway, a jetpack bomber with target rings. Lane enemies (skull minions) only guard detour crates.
Telegraphs: HANG, SWITCH and SWING prompts ~ 2-3 s before each new verb, fruit trails on the safe rail, the cart visible ~ 1.5 s ahead, bomber rings before impact (GP).
Each vertical tool gap teaches a different move: an arrow under a bounce crate (+3-4 u), crouch + double jump to a float-line (+4-5 u), a phase bounce crate + slide-jump to a ledge (+4-5 u).
The finale brings back the smallest footing (1 u steel boxes) in a vertical side view with phase toggles: an exam combining the level's two themes.
geometryTransfer: Rail posture chain: on a 25 s rail at 12-15 m/s (~ 300-375 m), place four steel obstacles at a 9.5 s interval, then 2.5 s and 2.5 s (~ 115-140 m, then ~ 30-38 m). The first gets a crate row 1.15 m lower beside the line as a second grind ledge; the later ones get a crate 1.2-1.5 m above the rail just past the obstacle.

Rail break: end the rail at a solid pillar and restart it 2.3-3.5 m later and ~ 0.6 m lower. A full ollie (~ 1.7 m high, ~ 0.64 s air) covers 7-9 m at grind speed, so breaks up to ~ 6 m stay fair; float a crate over the take-off.
Twin rails 2.3-3.5 m apart: alternate steel obstacles every ~ 1 s (12-15 m), put a fruit or crate trail on the free rail, then send an oncoming `mover` that is visible ~ 1.5 s (~ 20 m) ahead.
Rail exits: curl the rail end upward into a launch onto a checkpoint pad. Our skate landing wants >= 3 x 3 crates (3.5 m), larger than Crash's 2 x 2 u pad.
Delayed-lethal floor: a sand or `pit` zone whose ambusher surfaces 1-1.5 s after contact, crossed on 1.2 m round tops 1.2-2.3 m apart. On foot only: the board cannot land 1.2 m tops reliably.
Aimed strikes: a flying `sentry` that marks a 2-3 m ring under the player ~ 1.5 s before impact, used on a >= 5 x 4 crate platform that also holds an explosive puzzle.
